zebralogic.title: Interpret adjacency and ordering clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue uses terms like 'directly left of', 'directly right of', 'next to', or similar, enforce that the two referenced houses are adjacent in the specified direction.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue contains adjacency language (directly left/right, next to, immediately left/right).
zebralogic.example: Treating 'directly left of' as merely 'somewhere left of', allowing the houses to be non‑adjacent.

zebralogic.title: Interpret distance clues correctly
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states 'N houses between X and Y', enforce that exactly N other houses separate X and Y, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: Whenever a clue mentions a specific number of houses between two items.
zebralogic.example: Interpreting 'one house between X and Y' as X and Y being one house apart instead of two houses apart.

zebralogic.title: Treat 'somewhere left/right of' as inequality
zebralogic.principle: Interpret 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of' as a strict ordering constraint (pos(X) < pos(Y) or pos(X) > pos(Y)) without requiring adjacency.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue uses the phrasing 'somewhere left of' or 'somewhere right of'.
zebralogic.example: Assuming 'somewhere left of' means the two houses must be adjacent, placing X directly next to Y.

zebralogic.title: Enforce uniqueness across each attribute category
zebralogic.principle: Each value in a category must appear exactly once across all houses; no two houses may share the same value.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: After assigning any attribute, verify that the value has not already been used in another house.
zebralogic.example: Assigning the same music genre to two different houses.

zebralogic.title: Preserve original case of attribute values
zebralogic.principle: Copy attribute values exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving spelling and case.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When writing the final solution JSON.
zebralogic.example: Changing 'hip hop' to 'Hip Hop' or misspelling 'jazz' as 'jaz'.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for name‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: If a clue links a specific name to an attribute, enforce both directions: the name has that attribute and that attribute belongs to that name.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue directly associates a name with an attribute (e.g., 'Peter lives in a Victorian house').
zebralogic.example: Assigning the Victorian house to Peter but allowing another name to also be Victorian.

zebralogic.title: Bidirectional equivalence for attribute‑attribute clues
zebralogic.principle: When a clue states that two attributes belong to the same house, enforce that both attributes are assigned to the same house and that house's other attributes reflect this equivalence.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue links two non‑name attributes (e.g., 'The person who loves baseball also loves romance books').
zebralogic.example: Assigning baseball to Arnold but forgetting to also assign romance to Arnold.

zebralogic.title: Apply direct placement constraints
zebralogic.principle: If a clue explicitly places an attribute in a specific house number, enforce that placement exactly.
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When a clue mentions a specific house number (e.g., 'The basketball lover lives in house 4').
zebralogic.example: Ignoring that basketball must be in house 4 and placing it elsewhere.

zebralogic.title: Output solution JSON with exact schema and no extra text
zebralogic.principle: Emit only the JSON object with the required top‑level keys and structure; any extra characters cause parsing errors.
zebralogic.example: Including explanatory text like 'The solution is:' before the JSON.

zebralogic.title: Chain adjacency clues into consecutive blocks
zebralogic.principle: When multiple clues each state a direct left/right relationship that share an intermediate attribute, combine them to form a chain of consecutive houses (e.g., A left of B and B left of C implies A, B, C occupy consecutive positions).
zebralogic.when_to_apply: When adjacency clues involve overlapping attributes, creating a longer ordering chain.
zebralogic.example: Placing country music at house 1, hip‑hop at house 3, and biography at house 5, violating the required consecutive order.

zebralogic.description: Interpreting 'N houses between' as distance N
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model confuses the phrase 'N houses between X and Y' with a separation of N positions, forgetting that the distance in positions is N+1.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: When a clue says 'N houses between', enforce that exactly N other houses separate the two items, i.e., |pos(X) - pos(Y)| = N + 1.

zebralogic.description: Ignoring equivalence clues that bind two attributes to the same house
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may treat each clue independently and fail to propagate the equivalence, leaving the two attributes unlinked.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Whenever a clue links two attributes, record a bidirectional equivalence and ensure both are assigned to the same house.

zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may assign the same value to multiple houses when focusing on satisfying individual clues without checking global uniqueness.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Maintain a set of used values for each attribute category and reject any assignment that duplicates a value.

zebralogic.description: Altering attribute values (spelling/casing) instead of copying them verbatim
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model may normalize text or apply its own formatting, unintentionally changing the exact string required.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Copy attribute strings exactly as they appear in the problem statement, preserving case and spelling, and use them unchanged in the output.

zebralogic.description: Including extra explanatory text or stray characters outside the required JSON solution
zebralogic.why_it_happens: The model tends to add natural‑language commentary before or after the JSON, which the verifier cannot parse.
zebralogic.how_to_avoid: Produce only the JSON object with the required top‑level keys; do not prepend or append any other text.
